title: Construct an exact dyadic rank-seven P104 projector (no new kappa)
body:
Resolves PR #6211's dyadic-projector question: an explicit Hermitian projector over Z[i,1/2] has complex rank seven and maximum entry error 16193/65536 < 1/4 on the same 104-root Gram matrix. This removes odd denominators; it does not beat the predecessor's best complex error. **No new κ.**

Base: 2485805a6d47f36ea83ddde6327d453ac82d44dc. Predecessor #6211: 369ad15647ad0df0b0ef6f4fcb060509b67f1823. [Published proof, exact input pins, search coverage and validation](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/tree/18b1723ef87086d046358db6865a42df4dfd7555/research/p104-dyadic-rank-seven). Only this package is added.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12:
`python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-dyadic-rank-seven`
Expected: PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE.

Executed on Linux/Python 3.12.14: six registered normal/optimized checks; all 10,816 entries in each of two arithmetic paths; exact rank and dyadic checks; nine semantic and four source-byte rejection controls. Six Git-free/read-only replays agree, and two actual exported-byte corruptions reject. The bounded search stops at its first witness (k=8); no denominator/error optimality is claimed. Remote commit/tree and all 14 package/input files are checked against tested bytes.

The P104/root identification is inherited. Real-part rank remains eight; residual spectral norm remains 13. Native realization, caller, residual correction, dirty restoration and a favorable complete invoice remain open. The selected frontier and five framework assumptions are unchanged; no full multiplier or formal proof is claimed.

By @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit apoursh (#6211/#6191), Nick Petalas (#6183), Matarener (#6166), and the retained P104 lineage. Apache-2.0.
